answer: The grower counts the poles in every hop garden and weighs the pockets at the oast against the garden they came from. A nebula pocket bought from another grower fails the tally: at the jetty of the bine the hops must match the garden's own poles, and bought hops smell of another soil. Faking a harvest means renting a garden, tending bines for a season and paying 11,200, and the ivory entry in the bine tally is checked at every brewery, so hops whose garden was never counted are refused.
